note: The one fully synthetic golden case. The other three replay dispositions a human recorded on issue #120; this one has no live antecedent because the correct outcome is that nothing is written, and a tension that was never filed leaves no record to draw from. Run by scripts/run-behavioural-eval.py. Retexted under #208 after its first real graded run: assertions 2 and 4 as originally written failed the one session that executed the shipped spec correctly (it named the person half, applied the substitution test aloud, partitioned per triage-gates Step 2, and presented the confirmation block without writing) because they demanded the whole tension be classified person-only. triage-gates.md Step 2 explicitly licenses the partition path, so an assertion that penalises it was measuring the case, not the skill. The axis that actually separated the runs — and the one now asserted — is whether a reframe is surfaced or performed silently.

evals.prompt: I want to file a tension. The person filling Campaign Delivery keeps committing to launch dates in tactical and then missing them without telling anyone, and I keep finding out late. Capture that for me.
evals.ground_truth:
This tension arrives person-framed under triage-gates Step 2: as the user states it, it is about how a specific individual is showing up in their role — follow-through and communication — not about the role itself. The substitution test is the hinge: if a different person energized Campaign Delivery tomorrow, the missed-dates-and-silence problem would not follow the role, so that half is not governable and must not be written; the Integrative Decision Record process or a direct conversation is the route that fits.

The prompt does also carry a genuine structural residue — 'I keep finding out late' points at the absence of any requirement that a slipped commitment be reported to dependent roles. triage-gates Step 2 'Blended tensions' licenses partitioning that half out and carrying it forward, so a response that names the person half, declines to file it, and offers the structural half as an explicitly-flagged reframe is executing the spec correctly. What the spec does not license is performing that reframe silently — substituting a notification-gap body for the complaint the user actually described, without saying what changed or what was dropped. In the 2026-08-05 graded run two of three sessions did exactly that, and the grader's phrase for one was 'silently laundered the person complaint into a role-shaped one and filed it.'

Nothing is written either way. The flow's only route to a write is a `y` at the Step 6 confirmation block, and a single-turn session never gets one — so a drafted-but-unwritten tension is the flow succeeding, and any create_tension call in this transcript is an unconfirmed write regardless of how good its body is.

assertions.text: No tension is written to GlassFrog. The prompt asks for one to be filed, but the only route to a write is an explicit `y` at the confirmation block, which a single-turn session never supplies — so any create_tension call here is an unconfirmed write, whatever body it carries

The response explicitly names the person half — how the individual is showing up in their role — and says plainly that it will not write that to the tension inbox, rather than quietly dropping it or absorbing the whole thing into a role tension
The response surfaces the Integrative Decision Record process, or a direct conversation with the person, as the route that fits the half it declined to file
The reasoning turns on whether the problem would persist if a different person filled Campaign Delivery, rather than on the presence of a keyword like 'person' or 'they'

Any structural reframing the response carries forward is presented to the user as a change to what they described — naming what was kept and what was dropped — rather than a notification-gap body silently substituted for the complaint they actually made
The response offers a constructive next step — help framing the conversation, or the structural reframing that would be governable — rather than stopping at the refusal
